speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning after a rear-end collision; can you describe exactly how your leg looks and how it moved when the accident happened?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned pain in both knees, but your primary concern is the right groin pain; can you tell me if that right leg feels numb, tingling, or weak compared to the left? Also, has anyone noticed if your right knee is bent at an unusual angle or locked in place?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Central Dislocation of the Right Femoral Head.

The description of the right leg being shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated is the classic presentation of this injury. Can you confirm if you have lost the ability to bear any weight on that leg, and have you noticed any bruising on the buttock or perineum? REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_XRay
